text:
The expression is best read as a hybrid: an RSS-flavored account of the frozen warehouse prose, with seven explicit `PROSE-ESCAPE` fragments where RSS lacks primitives. It is not a single RSS formula, and it does not claim to be one. That is a legitimate disposition for the selected carrier. RSS is explicitly noncomputable and does not require a decision procedure, so the expression should not be faulted merely for failing to produce one. The more useful question is where the translation into RSS loses, adds, or hardens something relative to the frozen prose, and where the independent reading misstates the evidence.

The `PROSE-ESCAPE` quotations are exact against the frozen corpus. For example, the source has:

> “If different bookings have unresolved alternatives, availability is not a number but a set or an interval, and possibly not even a convex one.”

The expression quotes this exactly and marks the RSS obstruction correctly. The same is true of the partial-order conjecture, the possible-worlds criticism, the “better supported” sentence, the interval-correlation criticism, the lost-delivery sentence, and the union/intersection/single-replica-view question. So the escapes are not a fabrication or a paraphrase masquerading as quotation. That matters because the independent reading says, “The source quotations cannot be verified here because the source corpus field is withheld.” In this packet the corpus text is present, and the quotations can be verified. That is a defect in the probe or reader visibility, not in RSS or in the expression. The independent reading’s caution is therefore partly obsolete here.

The clearest lost distinction is the source’s assertion of shared coordinates. The source says:

> “The capacity and logical time are shared coordinates, but the records arrive as a bag…”

The expression instead says:

> “Take the described snapshot as a Viewpoint: a Coordinate (capacity, logical time) and a Bag of deliveries.”

Later the expression says:

> “different Viewpoints may have different logical times; if so, expiry is replica-relative—in RSS, viewpoint-relative.”

RSS defines a Coordinate as something that “can be shared or replica-relative” and treats coordinates as “parameters of a viewpoint, not as absolute facts.” So the expression’s move is RSS-native, but it weakens the source’s initial claim. A distinguishing case: two replicas have the same capacity and logical time but different bags. The source describes capacity and logical time as shared coordinates, so their sameness is part of the snapshot description. The expression’s Viewpoint framing permits their difference, and later explicitly contemplates different logical times across viewpoints. This is an introduced RSS commitment: coordinates are viewpoint parameters. It is not fatal, because RSS permits shared coordinates, but the expression does not preserve the source’s default. A proposed repair, not installed, would be to distinguish a shared coordinate from a viewpoint-relative coordinate, and to treat replica-relative time as a separate reading or conjecture rather than as the initial framing.

A second specific defect is the treatment of exact duplication. The source says:

> “Duplicate delivery of the same booking, revision, kind, quantity, and expiry adds nothing…”

The expression says:

> “Exact duplicate deliveries—same booking, revision, kind, quantity, expiry—add no authority…”

But RSS defines exact duplication as equality of “all record fields **and provenance**.” The expression uses the RSS term “Exact duplicate” while dropping the RSS provenance condition. A distinguishing case: two deliveries have the same booking, revision, kind, quantity, and expiry, but different provenance. Under the source’s wording, they are duplicates in the named fields and add no additional authority. Under RSS, they are not exact duplicates, because provenance differs. The expression’s phrasing therefore either narrows RSS or silently treats a source-level same-field duplicate as an RSS exact duplicate. This is a translator defect relative to the selected carrier, and the independent reading catches it. A repair would be to rename the source-level notion, for example “same-field duplicate,” and reserve “exact duplicate” for the RSS notion including provenance. That repair should be recorded, not installed.

A related but smaller loss is near-duplication. The source says:

> “if two records share booking and revision but differ in kind or quantity, are they duplicates or alternatives?”

The expression says:

> “two records sharing booking and revision but differing in kind or quantity are near-duplicates and candidates for Conflict…”

But RSS says near-duplication is when two deliveries “share booking and revision but differ in kind, quantity, **or expiry**.” The expression omits expiry. A distinguishing case: two records share booking and revision and have the same kind and quantity, but different expiry. The source’s exact-duplicate condition includes expiry, so they are not exact duplicates. RSS would call them near-duplicates. The expression’s paraphrase would not clearly classify them that way. This is a small but real lost distinction, and the repair is simply to include expiry in the near-duplicate description.

The next issue is supersession versus removal. The source says:

> “A higher revision kills lower revisions for that booking…”

and later:

> “group its records by revision, then keep only the greatest revision present.”

The expression repeats “supersedes” and “keeps only the greatest revision present.” RSS says supersession is “structural within a reading” and that lower revisions can remain in the Bag/Viewpoint as superseded stories. A distinguishing case is the one the source itself uses: revision 5 expired, revision 3 active. Under Reading A, revision 5 remains the chosen record but reserves zero, and revision 3 stays obsolete. Under Reading B, expiry deletes revision 5, so revision 3 becomes greatest and active. If “keeps only the greatest revision present” is read as removing lower revisions from the Bag, then Reading B cannot be represented as expiry deleting the high revision; one would have to restore the lower revision. The expression does preserve both readings as readings, so the defect is not total. But the phrase “keeps only” can blur the distinction between Bag membership and liveness/selection. The source itself uses that phrase, so the defect is partly inherited from the prose. Still, under RSS the translator should separate “remains in the Bag” from “is selected/live.” A proposed repair would be to say that lower revisions remain in the Bag but are superseded under Reading A, and that Reading B changes which record is treated as greatest by deleting or demoting the high revision.

Replication is another place where the translation substitutes an RSS primitive for a source notion. The source says:

> “It assumes logical current time is a single coordinate, but different replicas may have different logical times; if so, expiry is replica-relative.”

The expression says:

> “It assumes logical current time is a single Coordinate, but different Viewpoints may have different logical times; if so, expiry is replica-relative—in RSS, viewpoint-relative.”

RSS has no primitive for a replica. It has Viewpoints, Coordinates, Bags, Stories, Accounts, and Readings. A replica can be modeled as a Viewpoint, but not every Viewpoint is a replica. A distinguishing case: two observers with the same coordinate and the same bag but different trust in provenance are two Viewpoints but not two replicas. Conversely, two replicas that have merged identically might be one Viewpoint under discussion. The expression later flags the union/intersection/single-replica-view question as a `PROSE-ESCAPE`, which is the right move. But in the fourth disagreement it replaces “replica” with “Viewpoint” without marking that as a modeling assumption. This is a selected-language limitation: RSS lacks a replication primitive. It is not a failure of the source objection, and the prose escape keeps the objection admissible. A proposed repair would be to add an explicit modeling note or a relational primitive distinguishing replica from viewpoint, or to say “replica, modeled here as a Viewpoint.”

The expression’s handling of interval, convexity, partial order, possible worlds, evidential support, lost deliveries, and bag union/intersection is mostly honest. It marks them as `PROSE-ESCAPE` and states the RSS obstruction. This is exactly what the task permits: unsupported substantive content remains in ordinary prose. The selected carrier RSS does not have primitives for those notions, but that does not make the source’s objections impossible or inadmissible. It only means RSS cannot carry them as RSS relations. The expression does not falsely claim otherwise. The independent reading is right that the substantive criticism in those passages lives in prose, not in RSS, but that is not automatically a defect. It would become a defect only if the expression claimed those passages were RSS-native or if it dropped them. It does not.

There are several smaller introduced commitments. The expression says:

> “Availability is capacity minus whatever reservation is actually selected. In RSS, ‘actually’ signals a Reading.”

The source says:

> “Availability is then capacity minus whatever reservation is actually selected, but the word ‘actually’ hides the problem.”

Mapping “actually” to a Reading is RSS-native, but it may over-specify. A distinguishing case: someone might object not to the choice of expiry or tie-breaking policy, but to the assumption that there is a single actual selection at all. RSS can leave that as an open question, but the expression’s wording makes “Reading” the carrier of the problem. This is a mild over-assimilation rather than a lost distinction, because the expression later says no Reading is selected.

The expression also ends with:

> “this is not a failure of the reconstruction, but the only honest form the frozen text permits.”

The source ends with:

> “Keeping these disagreements visible is not a failure of the reconstruction; it is the reconstruction’s only honest form.”

The expression adds “the frozen text permits.” That is a normative attribution. The source’s claim is about the honesty of the reconstruction; the expression turns it into a claim about what the frozen text permits. RSS does not entail that the frozen text permits only this form. The independent reading flags this correctly. A repair would be to restore the source wording or to mark the sentence as a normative commitment rather than an RSS entailment.

The independent reading is otherwise largely accurate. It correctly identifies the main RSS-native machinery: Viewpoint, Coordinate, Bag, Story, Conflict, Reading, Projection, Account, Inquiry state. It correctly says no Reading is selected. It correctly notes that the expression treats negative availability as a signal, that it leaves release semantics open, that it leaves union/intersection/single-view open, and that it lacks a resource model. Its strongest criticisms are the provenance omission in exact duplication, the potential conflation of supersession with removal, and the substitution of Viewpoint for replica. Its weakest move is the claim that the source corpus is withheld; in this packet it is not. That is a probe/reader issue, not an RSS issue. Its claim that the final sentence is a normative commitment is also valid.

The defect loci can be summarized as follows. Translator defects: snapshot-to-Viewpoint substitution without preserving shared coordinates; exact-duplicate phrasing that drops RSS provenance; near-duplicate phrasing that drops expiry; possible blurring of Bag membership and supersession; and the added “frozen text permits” in the final sentence. Selected-language defects: RSS lacks primitives for replica, interval, convexity, partial order, possible worlds, evidential support, lost deliveries, and bag union/intersection. These are correctly marked as prose escapes, so they are not fatal to the expression. Reader/probe defects: the independent reading assumes the source is withheld and therefore cannot verify the `PROSE-ESCAPE` quotations, though they are exact in the packet. Compiler-bridge defects: none are evident; the expression is not claiming a Lean translation, and RSS is allowed to be noncomputable. The main bridge issue is that the expression sometimes uses RSS terms as labels for source-level notions that are not identical to RSS primitives, especially “exact duplicate.”

The unresolved disposition is that several competing readings remain live. On a charitable hybrid reading, the expression is a faithful exposure of the source’s uncertainty: it uses RSS where RSS can carry the content and prose escapes where it cannot. On a critical-limits reading, the expression shows that RSS is too weak for the warehouse problem: the substantive mathematical and replication content sits in the escapes, and RSS provides structure without deciding the hard cases. On an over-assimilation reading, the expression forces the source into RSS vocabulary and thereby introduces commitments about coordinates, duplicates, and readings that the source did not make. None of these readings is forced by the evidence. The proposed repairs are recorded but not installed: distinguish shared coordinates from viewpoint parameters; define same-field duplication separately from RSS exact duplication with provenance; include expiry in near-duplication; separate Bag membership from liveness; mark replica-to-Viewpoint substitution as a modeling assumption; and restore or qualify the final normative sentence. The source’s interval, convexity, partial-order, possible-worlds, support, lost-delivery, and bag-algebra objections remain admissible in ordinary prose even though RSS cannot encode them as RSS relations.
